# BTicino C300X Integration v2.3.0

## 2026-11-15

Version 2.3.0 is the direct stable update from 2.1.3, bringing the
complete display, media, configuration and reliability improvements developed
since that release. It also adds automatic visitor images. Version 2.2.0 was
withdrawn; it is neither required nor recommended as an intermediate upgrade.

## Visitor Images

- Save one visitor image after a doorbell ring or an active video session,
  including rings without an open dashboard. The device-wide **Save images**
  switch is on by default. Capture delay defaults to **5 seconds** and image
  retention to **14 days**, both configurable.
- Browse images in Home Assistant Media alongside recordings. The latest image
  appears as the card and camera preview, with the card identifying it as a
  saved image rather than a live view.
- Turning the switch off stops new captures and hides previews. Existing images
  remain in Media until they expire.
- The agent reads the existing camera framebuffer into memory. It does not save
  images or temporary files on the C300X. JPEG conversion, storage and cleanup
  run in HA. Each capture adds bounded CPU, RAM and network use on the device.
- Normal display-buffer page flips no longer discard a completed visitor image;
  framebuffer layout, format and ownership checks remain in place.

## Native Display

- Control **Touch tone** from **Configuration** on the C300X device page in HA
  with the Display patch active. The switch follows the original GUI setting
  and waits for confirmation instead of showing an assumed state.
- In the device's original **Settings → General**, keep **Tone buttons** and add
  **HA feedback colors** directly below it. The new switch defaults on and
  persists across restarts. Error texts and real alarm states remain visible;
  the original settings page is backed up and restored with the Display patch.
- Fix the Qt 4 startup crash introduced in 2.2.0: the memo retry timer belongs
  to the QML page instead of being created dynamically by shared JavaScript.
- Configure connection, media, activations, Alarmo, display, pages and tiles in
  separate settings areas. Tile sizes, names and secondary lines have translated
  labels and help. Arrange up to eight pages with names and connection status
  in the header; weather leads the status page.
- Control supported locks, vacuums, valves, humidifiers and water heaters.
  Unlocking or opening a lock requires confirmation. Automations and sirens
  use switch tiles; people and device trackers use read-only tiles.
- Media players gain compact transport, artist, shuffle and repeat controls.
  Lights expose effects and fans follow their supported speed grid.
- Preserve cleared fields, untitled pages and Alarmo settings across edits;
  refresh display events after agent restarts. Alarmo controls remain available
  when requesting an already active mode.
- Keep device-button registry entries when an offline device leaves its patch
  state unknown. Refresh display examples and setup instructions.
- Show the Alarm and Home Assistant home-page buttons automatically when their
  content is configured. Reserved positions keep the other buttons stable;
  temporary connection failures retain the last confirmed visibility.
  Configuration changes refresh the buttons without a GUI restart.

## Calls, Recordings and Recovery

- Wait for late H.264 parameters before starting an MP4 recording, within a
  fixed probing budget, instead of failing immediately on an ongoing ring.
- Convert extracted recording frames to full color range before JPEG encoding
  ([#106](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-bticino-c300x/issues/106)).
- Preserve `ring` and other technical event types on event entities, allowing
  type-filtered automations to match while retaining translated display labels
  ([#107](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-bticino-c300x/issues/107)).
- Improve WebRTC startup and teardown, early ICE handling, card ring previews
  and interrupted audio setup. Coordinate talkback with shutdown and respect
  advertised RTSP timeouts for Ring and Home Call playback.
- Preserve completed recordings and earlier clips after failures. Clean up
  cancelled workspaces, reject busy captures before answering, and bound speech
  analysis work and cleanup.
- Recover entities and memo lists after reconnects without idle polling.
  Transfer large memo lists within a fixed shared response budget.
- Keep the card editor's camera and device assignment consistent when several
  C300X devices are configured.
- Stop failed automatic preview transitions from retrying indefinitely, and
  prevent late failures from clearing a newer stream. Cancel obsolete codec
  refreshes during entry reloads.
- Prevent delayed media commands and audio-gain preparation from affecting
  replacement sessions after the integration reloads or unloads.
- Match notification blueprint events to the selected device, including rings
  without a camera entity. Existing customized blueprint copies are preserved;
  re-import the notification blueprint to receive this correction.
- Retry unfinished update steps and verify outcomes against device status.
  Wait through a temporary maintenance-busy response from startup status checks
  before preparing an update, without blindly repeating upload or apply.
  Preserve device-owned settings on SSH reinstall; sync installed files without
  syncing each staged upload chunk. Preserve customized blueprints, queued
  commands and pending configuration.
- Abort SSH reinstallation before replacing files if existing device
  configuration cannot be read reliably; do not replace it with defaults.
- Roll back failed GUI file updates and keep recovery backups if removal cannot
  verify restoration. Restore label-only patches too. Repair invalid boot links
  transactionally and report init failures.

## Security and Compatibility

- Keep saved keys out of forms, redact diagnostic addresses and bound debug
  output. Empty key fields retain credentials.
- Validate addresses, ports, numeric values, message IDs and webhook credentials;
  clean up webhook registrations after interrupted setup.
- Bound HTTP and RTSP resources, reserve connections for the local display,
  validate RTSP credentials and clear session keys on stop. Verify routing
  backups and release archive contents before use.
- Reserve RTSP capacity before allocating workers, create codec temporary files
  privately, and apply a shared deadline to each local media command.
- Prepare agent removal in private temporary directories and abort before
  device changes if staging fails.
- Verify the packaged native executable against a reviewed local-build hash and
  source digest. The release workflow verifies those bytes; it does not claim
  an independent rebuild using the private device sysroot.
- RTSP uses TCP interleaving; unsupported UDP requests are explicitly rejected.
  See the [security policy](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-bticino-c300x/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
  for local-network and separate RTSP credential requirements.
- Native HA camera two-way audio is optional, off by default and available only
  on HA 2026.11 or newer with its Labs feature enabled. Card talkback is unchanged.
- Required runtime checks use the official minimum/latest HA containers and
  their bundled FFmpeg, covering recording startup, JPEG output and event types.

## Upgrade

- Update the integration and its packaged native agent to **2.3.0**. The new
  framebuffer endpoint and updated display files require the rebuilt agent;
  updating only HA does not apply device-side changes.
- Reapplying an active Display patch restarts the GUI once.
- Requires Home Assistant **2026.10.0** or newer. CI tests that minimum and the
  latest stable HA. Keep existing entries and cards.

## Verification Scope

A physical, unanswered ring was recorded successfully through HA 2026.11.1:
one decodable MP4 and three full-range JPEGs, followed by normal idle cleanup.
The exact failing recording from #106 was not available; reporter confirmation
is still requested. The framebuffer source was checked read-only on hardware;
the latest snapshot-agent correction is covered by native regression tests, not
an end-to-end installation of that agent on the device.
